title: 5 Days in Montreal
subtitle: Old Montreal, Mount Royal & the Old Port
summary: A late-summer family road trip to Montreal in August 2024: smoked meat at Schwartz's, the views from Mount Royal, a boat ride, the Ferris wheel and a zipline at the Old Port, a ghost tour of Old Montreal, a ferry to Parc Jean-Drapeau and a bagel taste-off on the drive home.

glance.label: Bases
glance.value: Hyatt Place Saratoga/Malta (1 night on the way up), then Le Saint-Sulpice Hotel in Old Montreal (3 nights)

glance.label: Big tickets
glance.value: Le Petit Navire boat ride, La Grande Roue, MTL Zipline, the Old Montreal ghost tour, the ferry to Parc Jean-Drapeau

glance.label: Getting around
glance.value: Our car to get there, then on foot, Uber and the river ferry

glance.label: Don't forget
glance.value: Passports for everyone: we cross the Canadian border by car

intro: Montreal is close enough to drive, so we made it a family road trip. We left after work on Wednesday, slept in Saratoga County to break up the drive, and were in Old Montreal by lunchtime on Thursday. Le Saint-Sulpice Hotel, beside the Notre-Dame Basilica, put us within walking distance of almost everything we wanted to do.

Each day had one anchor. Thursday was the classic first-timer's loop: smoked meat at Schwartz's, a walk up Mount Royal for the views, the Museum of Fine Arts and an evening on Place Jacques-Cartier. Friday stayed at the Old Port with a boat ride, the Ferris wheel and a zipline for the boys, then a ghost tour after dinner. Saturday we took the ferry across to Parc Jean-Drapeau for a food festival before an evening in the Village.

We booked the dinners and the timed activities ahead and kept a rain plan and a few backup ideas in our pocket. On the way out of town on Sunday we settled the great Montreal bagel argument for ourselves.

days_plan.label: Day 1
days_plan.title: Head north and break up the drive
days_plan.text: A short evening drive to get a head start, so Thursday morning is only the last few hours to the border and Montreal.

items.text: Leave home and drive to the Hyatt Place Saratoga/Malta
Check in at the Hyatt Place Saratoga/Malta and relax for the night

days_plan.tip: Before leaving the house, make sure everyone has their passport. You need one for each person to cross into Canada by car.

days_plan.label: Day 2
days_plan.title: Schwartz's, Mount Royal & an evening in Old Montreal
days_plan.text: We arrive around lunchtime and spend the afternoon on foot: lunch on the Plateau, a climb up Mount Royal for the views over the city, the Museum of Fine Arts on the way back down, then dinner at the Old Port.

items.text: Breakfast at the hotel
Leave the hotel and drive to Montreal, crossing the border on the way
Arrive at Le Saint-Sulpice Hotel, 414 Rue Saint-Sulpice, check in and head out for lunch
If it's raining: lunch in the Underground City, then the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts
If it's dry: walk to Schwartz's Deli, 3895 Boulevard Saint-Laurent, for Montreal smoked meat sandwiches for lunch. It's a long walk, so take an Uber if we're really hungry
If the line at Schwartz's is too long, walk about a mile to La Banquise for poutine instead, then walk around La Fontaine Park next door
After Schwartz's, walk up into Mount Royal Park: the Kondiaronk Belvedere, the big paved lookout in front of the Mount Royal Chalet, for the best photo over downtown, then on to Beaver Lake
Walk down to the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (Musée des beaux-arts de Montréal, open 10 AM to 5 PM)
Walk back to Le Saint-Sulpice Hotel along Saint Catherine Street
If we still have time and energy: Uber to the Biodôme or the Montreal Botanical Garden (both open 9 AM to 6 PM)
Walk to Place Jacques-Cartier, a lively square with street performers and cafés
Dinner at Vieux-Port Steakhouse & Terrasse
End the day with a slow walk along the Old Port promenade to see the city lights

days_plan.tip: Watch the forecast. The Underground City and the Museum of Fine Arts make an easy rainy-day swap for the walk up Mount Royal.

days_plan.label: Day 3
days_plan.title: Boat, Ferris wheel & zipline at the Old Port, then a ghost tour
days_plan.text: A day at the water's edge. Everything at the Old Port is a short walk from the next thing, so we line up the boat ride, the Ferris wheel and the zipline back to back, then wander Bonsecours Market and Rue Saint-Paul before dinner and a ghost tour after dark.

items.text: Walk to breakfast at a café nearby: Olive et Gourmando or Le Petit Dep
Arrive at the Old Port for our 11:00 AM boat ride on the river with Le Petit Navire
Ride La Grande Roue de Montréal, the big Ferris wheel at the Old Port. We printed our tickets for four
Tyrolienne MTL Zipline for the boys. The tickets aren't for a set time, so we go whenever it suits
See the Clock Tower and Clock Tower Beach
Lunch or snacks around Bonsecours Market
Stroll Rue Saint-Paul from east to west, Old Montreal's oldest street
Back to the hotel to get ready for dinner
Dinner at Gaspar Brasserie Française
Walk to the meeting point for the ghost tour
Old Montreal ghost tour through the old streets after dark

days_plan.tip: Get to Le Petit Navire about 20 minutes early. The Ferris wheel and the zipline are right next to each other, so the rest of the morning falls into place.

days_plan.label: Day 4
days_plan.title: Ferry to Parc Jean-Drapeau & a night in the Village
days_plan.text: We cross the river by ferry to Parc Jean-Drapeau, the island park left over from Expo 67, to see the Biosphère and catch Les Rendez-vous gourmands, a one-day food festival for the park's 150th anniversary, and try our luck at the Casino de Montréal. Back in town, we walk the car-free stretch of Saint Catherine Street East before dinner.

items.text: Leave for breakfast at a café nearby
Walk to the ferry dock at the Old Port and be there 15 minutes early
Ferry across to Parc Jean-Drapeau
Walk around the park: Espace 67 and the Biosphère. The free Discovery Ride trams go across the island if we get tired of walking
Les Rendez-vous gourmands in the Floralies Gardens, 25 Chemin des Floralies: an outdoor food festival with chefs, tastings, barbecues and music, on from noon to 11 PM
Back at the ferry dock for the 4:00 PM ferry to the Old Port. Roads run close to the gardens, so an Uber back to the hotel works if we want to leave earlier or stay later
Freshen up at the hotel if we're tired
Walk to Saint Catherine Street East in the Village, closed to cars between Saint-Hubert and Papineau, with shops, food and street entertainment
Dinner at Jacopo
If we're still up for it: the bars on Crescent Street

days_plan.tip: If the Village is too much fun to leave, cancel the Jacopo reservation on OpenTable in time and eat there instead.

days_plan.label: Day 5
days_plan.title: Bagel wars on the way home
days_plan.text: A slow morning, then the most important decision of the trip. Montreal has two famous bagel bakeries a few blocks apart in Mile End, and we stop at both on the drive out to see which one wins.

items.text: Check out of Le Saint-Sulpice Hotel
Bagel wars: drive to Mile End and compare the bagels from Fairmount Bagel and St-Viateur Bagel
Drive home

days_plan.tip: Buy an extra dozen of the winner for the car. Montreal bagels are best warm, but they're still good the next morning.

tips.title: Passports for everyone
tips.text: Driving into Canada means a border crossing, and every person in the car needs a passport. Check them before you leave home, not at the hotel the night before.

tips.title: Break up the drive
tips.text: Leaving after work and sleeping halfway meant we reached Montreal by lunchtime on Thursday with a full afternoon ahead of us, instead of losing the whole first day to the car.

tips.title: Stay in Old Montreal
tips.text: From Le Saint-Sulpice we walked to the Old Port, Place Jacques-Cartier, Rue Saint-Paul and most of our dinners. We used Uber for the farther sights, like the Biodôme and the Botanical Garden.

tips.title: Have a rain plan
tips.text: The Underground City links shops and food courts below downtown, and the Museum of Fine Arts is nearby. Both are good swaps for a wet afternoon.

tips.title: Look for the summer pedestrian streets
tips.text: In summer, Montreal closes several streets to cars, including Saint Catherine Street East in the Village. Check the city's list before you go for more places to wander.

tips.title: More ideas for a Saturday with kids
tips.text: The Geordie Family Fair was on that Saturday from 11 AM to 6 PM, free and about a 15-minute drive from Old Montreal. Check for family events on the dates you visit.
